chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Muthanna, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman who does not menstruate except every three or four years. He said: She observes a waiting period of three months, then she may marry if she wishes.

The correct interpretation of this report is that it applies to a woman who has no regular menstrual habit or has forgotten her habit; for her, the waiting period is three months, and her status is established by that. The earlier reports apply to a woman who had a regular habit that then changed; in that case, she should act according to her habit during the period of regularity.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman who menstruates only every few years?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq’s ruling for a woman with irregular menstruation (*al-mustahaddah*) who observes a three-month waiting period (*iddah*) before remarriage. The commentary distinguishes between women who have never established a regular cycle and those whose established cycle has changed, prescribing adherence to the previous stable pattern in the latter case. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic principle of relying on *'adah* (habitual pattern) to determine purity and impurity periods when the standard monthly cycle is disrupted.
